View of the Gyantse Kumbum, part of Palcho Monastery. People on the street in the foreground and walls of Gyantse Dzong (fortress) visible in the distance.
A woman wearing a necklace, earrings and nose-ring sitting, looking towards the camera at a market in Gyantse.

Full-length portrait of a man in shackles standing on rocks. According to the caption the man is a 'criminal' and 'awaiting his portion', referencing the distribution of alms to the poor of Gyantse on the occasion of the death of King George V.
A man distributing alms to a woman on the occasion of the death of King George V, captioned 'a hand out for the poor'.

View of people gathered for the distribution of alms on a stone parapet, many of them looking in the direction of the camera. The distribution of alms to the poor of Gyantse took place on the occasion of the death of King George V. An open plain and mountains visible in the distance.

The eastern courtyard, Deyang shar, of the Potala palace during New Year celebrations possibly taking place on the 29th day of the 12th month, the votive offering of the twenty ninth day, Tse gutor. Windows are hung with bright valances and the uppermost, the private room of the Dalai Lama, is curtained with yellow silk. Officials stand on lower balconies and entranceway to the palace watching the ceremony take place.

The eastern courtyard, Deyang shar, of the Potala palace. Two rings of masked dancers are performing a ritual dance. The dancers of the outer circle are wearing black hats, shva nag, and those of the inner circle are wearing animal masks. Two monks are standing in the centre (to the left of the scene) with a small table between them on which ritual implements have been placed.  A tiger-skin carpet is on the ground in front of them. The enthroned figure (behind which spectators are gathered) is a masked representation of Chinese priest Hashang who presides over the dance. There is an appliquéd awning to the right of the scene where a monk orchestra is seated on padded seats. An open parapet provides an upper viewpoint for spectators. This ceremony was part of the New Year celebrations possibly taking place on the 29th day of the 12th month, the votive offering of the twenty ninth day, Tse gutor.
Crowd of people gathered during the distribution of alms to the poor of Gyantse on the occasion of the death of King George V. Others are crossing a small stone bridge in the foreground.

A group of Tibetans with donkeys awaiting their turn to board a raft-like ferry to cross the Yarlung Tsangpo (an upper tributary of the Brahmaputra River). One of the travellers holds a dog tethered using a rope. A settlement is visible on the opposing riverbank.
Four Tibetan men in robes standing in a garden, possibly of Dekyi Lingka. An appliquéd canvas is hung behind them and a building is partially visible through vegetation.
Two seated Tibetan women looking through magazines in gardens, possibly of Dekyi Lingka.

Members of the Sakya royal family in the gardens of the British Mission, Dekyi Lingka. Gyalmo Dechen Drolma Sakya, the wife of HH Sakya Tri Rinpoche, is wearing an ornate Bagor headdress and ga'u amulet box around her neck. Another two members of the Sakya family are to the left and right of the scene. Attendants are visible behind.
A Tibetan baby sitting on a rug in gardens.
A Tibetan woman standing, looking towards the camera near a farmstead on the Zamzar Plains, believed to be a short hike away from Lhasa.

Jigme Taring (left), Colonel James Hislop (middle) and another high-ranking official with fur hat sitting, looking towards the camera with tea laid out on a table in front of them. A Tibetan man and woman stand behind them.
Postcard showing a pasture in northern Tibet.
Full-length portrait of a Tibetan official standing in silk robes.

Tibetan men seated at a table with stacks of ceremonial food laid out on the table in front of them.  Brocade decorates the back wall and there are paper decorations above it.  There is a brocade hanging from the ceiling with a paper decoration suspended from the  middle of it.  Rai Bahadur Norbu Dhondup sits at the head of the table on a chair decorated with brocade.  He is wearing a ceremonial silk brocade costume and round fur hat.  The other men on the left are all without hats and are guests. The man on the extreme left is wearing spectacles. The food on the table looks like fried bread (kabze) eaten at the time of the New Year.

Man, woman (holding a baby) and girl standing outside the British hospital in Lhasa.  There is also a dog sitting at the doorway.  The man seems very tall and is wearing a hat and a robe with a decorative border at the neck which includes a tie-die, cross pattern.  The girl's robe also has this cross pattern.
Kampa dancers disrobing after their performance outside the Dekyi Lingka.  There are a number of children among their number.  Trees in the background.

Review of the military escort at Gyantse comprising mounted and infantry contingents of the 1/15th Punjabis. The two figures in topees on the far left could be Basil Gould and either the Escort Commander, Major J.G Innes-Keys in command of the 1/15th Punjabis or the British Trade Agent, Gyantse who was, at that time, Hugh Richardson.

Taking tea at the Doring house.  Doring's wife is sitting behind a man sitting at the table. Dingja is on the right.  The table is laid with a tablecloth, cups and saucers (European style) and an assortment of cakes and sweets.  A window fitted with glass panes in a diamond pattern is in the background.  Also, there is a group of children in the background (left).
The Tsarong house in Lhasa.  A man (possibly S.A.S Rai Sahib Tonyot Tsering) and two women (Rinchen Dolma (Mary) Taring on the right) are standing near the front entrance.
The main entrance to the Jokhang.  There are monks and laypeople in the courtyard. The lamp post is clearly visible on the right.

Group of Tibetan and British officials standing in front of ponies.  From left to right, Tibetan orderly, unidentified, Pemba Tsering, Rai Bahadur Norbu Dhondup, Sonam Tobden Kazi, Capt. D.J. Thornburgh, Major J.G. Innes-Keys and Harry Staunton.  They are all dressed for cold weather with scarves and fur hats.
